headline: Binance withdrawals stay paused while it buys back the last of the stolen coins, ahead of a planned phased restart on Sunday and a reserve report due by Monday.

market.asOf: BTC, ETH and SOL from CoinMarketCap at about 11:57 UTC Sat 31 Oct (18:57 Bangkok); Fear and Greed from alternative.me, read at the same time. Check the live prices at the top of the page.
market.fearGreed: 30 out of 100 ('Fear') on alternative.me's Crypto Fear and Greed Index, down from 51 ('Neutral') the day before.

stories.title: Binance buys back stolen coins; withdrawals still paused ahead of Sunday restart
stories.summary: Withdrawals remain paused and no source found by this edition shows the reserve snapshot or Proof of Reserves results (a public check that customer balances are fully backed) have been published. Binance is buying back the stolen tokens it does not already hold, with a phased restart targeted for around 12:33 Bangkok time on Sunday 1 Nov, subject to security checks.
points: Binance has set aside more than $6.34B; about $5B (80%) of the stolen assets are already covered and about $1.3B is being bought on the market and in OTC (private) deals, per Bitcoin.com News.
Ethena sent 128.63M ENA (about $24M) to Binance, about 59% of the 217.5M ENA stolen; Binance will also repurchase 3.38B stolen RSR, per Bitcoin.com News.
Per ChainCatcher, Binance said it would 'gradually restore withdrawal services within approximately 34 hours', putting the restart at about 13:33 (UTC+8) on 1 Nov.
Binance has promised a full Proof of Reserves report by Monday 2 Nov, and the FBI and Secret Service are involved, per Investing.com.
Critics say a snapshot taken after the buyback could hide how big the gap was; claims of an inside job on social media have no hard evidence behind them, per Bitcoin.com News.

stories.title: The hack becomes an election-week political fight in Washington
stories.summary: With the US midterm elections on Tuesday 3 Nov, top officials and lawmakers are using the Binance hack to argue about how crypto should be regulated.
points: Asked about the hack, President Trump said 'We don't know. We're looking at that,' per Cointelegraph.
Senator Cynthia Lummis said the stalled Clarity Act would have let firms freeze suspicious funds quickly; the bill failed to advance on 15 Sept, per Cointelegraph.
CFTC Chairman Mike Selig said the hack supports the agency's proposed rules and that offshore exchanges lack US-style safeguards, per Cointelegraph.
Rep. Maxine Waters called the hack a 'wake-up call' and pointed to Binance's ties to the Trump family, in a 30 Oct statement.

sources.label: House Financial Services Democrats: Waters statement

stories.title: Stolen bitcoin still parked as markets head into a weak October close
stories.summary: Blockchain trackers give slightly different totals for how much was stolen and frozen, so each is named. The stolen bitcoin has not moved, and US spot bitcoin and ether funds saw money leave in the latest session.
points: Amount stolen: Elliptic says $6.43B, TRM Labs $6.36B and Binance about $6.3B.
Frozen: Elliptic says $2.85B; TRM Labs said $2.7B as of 30 Oct. Elliptic says the attacker still holds 519,104 ETH and 18,270 BTC.
CoinDesk says the 18,270 stolen BTC sits in 19 addresses, more than Tesla's 11,509 BTC, and none had been spent as of 2:02am ET Friday.
US spot bitcoin ETFs had net outflows of about $643M on 30 Oct and spot ether ETFs about $156M, per TokenPost; Saturday is not a trading day, so Monday brings the next figures.
Cointelegraph, citing CoinGlass, said bitcoin was set to close October 7.7% lower, its worst October since 2014.

briefs.title: Chainalysis reports its own data breach
briefs.summary: Chainalysis said attackers accessed customer names, emails, user IDs and job titles, and that the breach is unrelated to the Binance hack, per TokenPost.

briefs.title: Liquidations cool to about $400M
briefs.summary: About $403.67M of leveraged bets were liquidated over 24 hours, 76.48% of them longs, per Koin Bülteni's Saturday market overview.
